file.name: SketchfabRipper.exe
file.type: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64 Mono/.Net assembly, for MS Windows

strings: !This program cannot be run in DOS mode.
GEnter an URL to download from.
Supported links are listed in README.md.
Converts models to a usable format using Blender. Disabling will allow faster downloads, but manual conversion will be required later.

Will not show any prompts requiring user interaction during the download and conversion process. Existing models will be skipped by default, downloads will not be retried and error messages will not be displayed.
Suppresses any errors or prompts requiring user interaction. Useful for batch downloads, where prompts and errors would otherwise interrupt the queue.

Best for archival purposes. Will download and keep all files created during conversion, including textures, sounds, backgrounds, environment data, animations in .bin/.action format, model .osgjs/.bin files, JSON metadata etc. Uses most disk space and has the longest download times.

Best for converting or updating at a later date. Will download and keep all generated and most original files, including materialInfo.txt, .bin/.osgjs files, JSON metadata etc. Will not download additional data such as environments, backgrounds and sounds.
Same as the "Extras" option, but also removes generated files such as materialInfo.txt and animations in .action format, keeping only original Sketchfab data and the converted model.
The default option. Removes everything but textures, the converted model and thumbnail. Uses less disk space while keeping all essential files.
Removes everything but the converted model after conversion, including textures. Uses least disk space but produces an incomplete rip. Best for 3D printing, where textures are not needed.
Appends a unique ID to the name of each downloaded model to avoid filename conflicts. May appear cluttered, especially in folders containing a lot of models.
MModels are converted without rigs or animations. Compatible with most models.
Models are converted preserving the original bone data. Compatible with some models, may cause broken or missing geometry on others.

Models are converted with animations. Each animation is saved to a separate FBX file. Some animations may appear broken, possible fixes have been posted in the Discord server. Uses a modified version of the "Rigged" mode script, and is incompatible with some models.
vUses different Blender scripts to convert downloaded models. Try changing this if your models fail to export properly.
eThe most compatible option. Can easily be imported using most 3D modelling software and game engines.
Best for PBR materials. Most materials can be exported properly, while being compatible with more software than .blend files. Animations not yet supported.
sBest for 3D printing. Note that several features are unsupported while using OBJ mode, such as rigs and animations.
qSkips converting the model and saves the .blend file after the model has been imported using the Blender scripts.

Saves a .blend file in addition to the standard model. Enabling this is highly recommended when using the "Additional processing" option since the .blend files preserve PBR materials, while formats other than glTF only support albedo/normal maps.
wModel output format. FBX recommended as it is smaller and supports more features than OBJ. FBX is required for rigging.
Sends each converted model to its start pose. Useful for animated/rigged models which you don't want in a T/A-pose, but may cause bone rotation issues.
Checked: Model is sent to its start pose.
Filled: Two models are saved - one is sent to its start pose, the other is not.
Unchecked: Model is not sent to its start pose.

Attempts to convert triangles in downloaded models to quads, using a built-in Blender feature. The result is saved to a new file with the suffix ".quads.fbx" and/or ".quads.blend". Will not restore a model's original topology, but can help approximate it. Requires "Additional processing" to be enabled.

Automatically applies materials and vertex colours to each model, and fixes vertex normal issues. Also renames meshes and materials to their original names (if present in file.osgjs/model_info.json). Enabling "Save .blend" is recommended. May fail when models have a large number (10,000,000+) of polygons.
Places all downloaded models into a subfolder with the artist's username. Enabling this option is recommended when downloading a large number of models from the same artist.
IPackaged files will remain in the "_packaged" folder and not be uploaded.
Upload packaged files to ZippyShare. Does not require registration. 500 MB/file limit, larger archives will automatically be split. Links will be saved to "_zippyshareLinks.txt".
Upload packaged files to a Telegram chat. Requires registration, . 2 GB/file limit, larger archives will automatically be split.
vAutomatically compresses each downloaded model to a .zip file located in "_packaged". Recommended when uploading rips.

Authenticate Sketchfab requests with a session ID instead of an access token. Session IDs allow original archives to be downloaded, unlike access tokens which only provide generated glTF/USDZ files. Session IDs can be obtained from your web browser's cookie storage after logging in to Sketchfab. If a session ID and access token are already present in SketchfabRipper.ini, changing this will switch between them.
